enrichments.description:
Over a century ago, Akaza was a human by the name of |Hakuji}}, a prodigious martial artist who trained under Keizo while nursing his daughter, Koyuki, who would later become his fiancée.

Akaza was a very muscular young man of average height with skin so fair it appeared bright green-tinged white, decorated by a pattern of thick blue lines, which resembled the criminal tattoos he had as a human. He had short, cerise hair that fluffed out around his head and inward-tilting yellow eyes with cerise eyelashes and blue sclera that somewhat resembled cracked glass. The kanji for |Jōgen}} was etched into his right iris, and the daiji for |San}} was etched into his left.

The lines on his face curved through each of his eyes from below his ears to over his temples, another blue line running from the center of his hairline to the bridge of his nose, with two more lines running around his neck, three others branching off the lower one to his torso. The middle line ran directly down his chest to halfway down his stomach, and the other two branched off to the sides over each side of his chest to join the two other lines. This same three-line pattern also repeated around his waist. On his arms, lines were running down the front of his shoulders that ran into two more, which went around his biceps before continuing to run down to his wrists, below which each of his fingers was also dark blue with an orange fingernail. His toes and toenails also sharing this unusual appearance as his fingers and fingernails.

Akaza only sported a short, sleeveless dark purple-pink haori cut off at his waist, left open to expose his chest, and decorated by a square pattern on his back. Below this, he sported a pair of baggy white pants that he rolled to just below the knee with a turquoise rope belt to secure them at his waist, with bright pink tassel ornaments hanging on the front and the back of the rope belt. Akaza preferred to go barefoot but wore a pair of chains of large, round, red pearls around his ankles.

enrichments.description:
Enmu was a slender young man of pale skin complexion who appeared to be in his mid twenties. He possessed a medium build and was of average height. He had ringed blue eyes that tilted sharply down towards the sides of his face, the left one of which had the kanji for |Ka}} and daiji for |Ichi}} etched into its iris, and a horizontal goat-like slit on his right instead of a pupil. He had three square-shaped markings on each of his cheeks, each separated by a smaller square, which fade from green to yellow in color, and straight chin-length black hair which he wore parted to his right, the right side tucked behind his ear. His hair faded into a red-pink color near the ends, but appeared blue at the tips of the two longer, shoulder-length strands that curve upwards and outwards below the base of his neck, from under the rest of his hair.

Enmu wore a long, black button-up coat that arched upwards on either side of his legs so that only the two tails in front and behind fell down below his knees, and a white dress shirt, the cuffs of which appeared over those of his coat. He also wore a pair of pinstriped pale gray pants and white heeled shoes.

When Enmu received more blood from Muzan Kibutsuji, his left hand formed a mouth at the back, an eye next to it and most of his fingers had the kanji for |Yume}} etched on their skin. In addition, his face had several noticeably veins popping out.

Enmu was cold, callous, and sadistic, openly stating that he enjoyed the pain and suffering of humans. His favorite method of torment was giving them a happy and pleasant dream before turning it into a nightmare and taking pleasure in the agonized expressions they made as he tortured them. This sadism even extended to his fellow demons, as he relished seeing his fellow Lower Ranks being killed right in front of his eyes. In contrast to his depravity, Enmu was also effeminate and soft-spoken. He spoke with a tender tone and frequently referred to humans as his "child".

enrichments.description:
Giyu is a fairly tall young man of a lean muscular stature and pale complexion, consistently seen wearing a stoic expression. He has raven-black hair of uneven lengths, with jaw length side-bangs, a low messy ponytail at the base of his neck, and bangs falling over his eyes in a choppy fringe. His eyes are sharp and moderately large; his irises are lapis blue that fades into a lighter shader at the lower part, surrounded navy blue pupils. His irises are sometimes completely opaque and empty. His eyes are framed by thin eyebrows.

Giyu wears the standard Demon Slayer Corps uniform, colored black in the manga and tinted charcoal blue in the anime. It consists of a button-up jacket with a stand-up collar and long sleeves. Additionally, it features gold buttons and a shirt pocket on the left breast, with the kanji for |Metsu}} engraved on the back of the uniform. Beneath the jacket, he wears a white long-sleeved collared undershirt. The uniform is fastened at the waist with a white belt and includes a pair of matching tattsuke-hakama pants, wrapped at the calves with buttoned white kyahan. On his feet, he wears tabi socks that match the tone of his uniform, along with white zōri sandals with navy blue straps. Over this, Giyu wears a distinctive haori that is split down the middle into two contrasting halves - the right half being a carmine color, the left half decorated in a traditional geometrically patterned rhombi consisting of green, dark green, orange, and yellow. These haori halves are sentimental mementos, with the red side formerly belonging to his late older sister, Tsutako Tomioka, and the patterned side to his deceased friend and fellow apprentice, Sabito.

During the Demon Slayer Corps' battle against Muzan Kibutsuji, Giyu loses his right arm. Following the fight, Giyu cuts his hair down to neck length. He is seen wearing a button-up collared shirt under a kimono with umanori hakama pants.

While Giyu was training under Sakonji Urokodaki, he wore a dark red haori which would later make up his current one as well as black tucked-in tattsuke-hakama pants. He also wore his current white leg-wrapped kyahan and pair of white zōri with dark blue straps. In addition, he wears the warding masks that are signature to Sakonji's pupils. For Giyu, it is a white fox mask with light blue eyes.

enrichments.description:
Inosuke is a young man of average height and pale skin complexion with an extremely toned and muscular build for his age. In sharp contrast to this, he has an incredibly pretty and feminine face, which made Zenitsu almost believe that he was a girl. He has large, wide eyes that are framed by an array of long eyelashes, their iris a dark to soft pale green with black pupils that has a small, white dot on the center of the pupils, thin eyebrows, and what could be a small, well-mannered mouth. His thick, raven-black hair reaches just past his shoulders, fading into blue at the tips and forming an unruly and uneven fringe that falls just above his eyes, puffing out before curving and thinning towards his forehead.

Inosuke, in his unique fashion, has customized his Demon Slayer uniform to suit his personal style. His altered attire consists of baggy hakama pants in a dark gray-blue shade, secured at his hips with a thick belt adorned with fluffy brown deer fur. Unlike his fellow companions, Inosuke forgoes wearing a haori. Instead of the customary leg wraps, he opts for knee-high socks made from bear hide in a black color tone, which serve as a base for the sandals he wears. Notably, his heels and toes are left exposed. However, the most distinctive aspect of his appearance is the gray, hollowed-out boar's head that he wears as a mask, with sky blue eyes with darker blue irises and black pupils, a pink snout, and a shade of pink on both of the upper portion of the ears. Inosuke has modified the boar's head, altering the eyes to allow him to see while wearing it.

Inosuke is short-tempered, confrontational, abrasive, and proud. He always likes to think he is the strongest fighter in a situation, constantly challenging most people he comes across and wanting others to respect and praise him for his skill. This often leads him into unnecessary danger since he tends to overestimate his abilities in comparison to who he is fighting and refuses to accept when he has been defeated, which can be seen when Giyu Tomioka has to tie him up after his fight with Father of the Spider Family to prevent him challenging the Hashira while still severely injured from his previous battle. This constant wanting to be the best can also cause Inosuke to be very provocative, as he often tries to goad others, most prominently Tanjiro Kamado, into fighting him, although in the case of the latter he usually fails due to Tanjiro's obliviously kind nature.

enrichments.description:
Kanao is a young woman of short stature, with large and gentle eyes of a dark lilac color that turns to a lighter color at the lower of the irises and a purple center along with notable bright light reflecting, that are framed by thick eyelashes, and pink lips in contrast to her pale complexion. She has medium-length, thin raven-black hair, tied into a side ponytail on the right of her head and fastened by a green butterfly ornament with a pink trim on the outer side of the wings, and decorated with white speckled spots, that once belonged to her adoptive sister Kanae. She has straight cut bangs, a straight fringe, and two loose, chin-length strands that curve downwards from above each of her ears.

Kanao wears a slightly purple-tinted variation of the standard Demon Slayer uniform, consisting of a button-up jacket with a stand-up collar and long sleeves, featuring silver buttons and a shirt pocket on the left breast, with the kanji for |Metsu}} engraved on the back of the uniform. Beneath the jacket, she wears a white long-sleeved collared undershirt. Rather than the traditional tattsuke-hakama pants, her uniform is customized with a knee-length pleated skirt in the same tinted color, secured with a white belt around her waist. Over time, however, the skirt was noticeably shortened to only cover her thighs, a modification implied to be the work of the notoriously lecherous uniform tailor, Masao Maeda. Draped over her uniform, she wears a short white cloak, fastened on one side by a dark pink triple knot. On her feet, she sports distinctive knee-high lace-up white boots with tan soles, heels, and toes. During the Final Selection, she wore a light pink yukata stop a white undershirt and a magenta pair of hakama pants. She also wore white ankle socks and pink sandals.

When she was a young child living in poverty, Kanao had severely disheveled hair, and a tattered and dirty pink kimono with lighter circular patterns. It is also worth noting that despite likely being a preteen around 12 years old, she was abnormally short and had the appearance of a younger child due to severe malnutrition stunting her growth.

Sometime between then and her next appearance in the Infinity Castle, the color of Kanao's hair changes, with the ends being slightly tinted purple, fading to a neon pink halfway down her ponytail. After her battle with Doma, Kanao begins to wear Shinobu's hairpin rather than Kanae's, as her's was shattered during the battle. She also loses much of the vision of her right eye due to her using Flower Breathing's final form to take out the Upper Rank with her eye gaining a defined pupil with a dark ring around it and becoming deprived of its gradient.

In order to become a Demon Slayer, an individual must pass Final Selection, a test used as an entrance exam to join the Demon Slayer Corps. During this selection, examinees must survive for seven days on the mountain top of Mount Fujikasane, a perilous domain infested with demons. The examinees must rely solely on the skills they have developed in training. The majority of candidates participating in the Final Selection have undergone extensive training under the guidance of a cultivator of a Breathing Style. Only when these candidates have reached a satisfactory level of skill and competence, are they entrusted by their Cultivator to partake in the selection. The author of the series uses a pen name and has chosen to maintain anonymity by not disclosing their gender. To represent themselves in public announcements related to the series, the author uses an avatar of an alligator wearing glasses, which has become their distinctive symbol. While the author, under the pen name Gotoge, has not personally revealed their gender for privacy reasons, it was allegedly revealed by an anonymous Weekly Shonen Jump employee that the author is a woman. Kohei Ohnishi, an editor at Weekly Shonen Jump, has also said that the writer's personality shines through the series, in particular in Tanjiro Kamado's "serious nature, honesty, and strong sense of responsibility".

Gotoge was born in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, on May 5, 1989.

At the age of 24, Gotoge participated in the 70th Jump Treasure Newcomer Manga Awards in 2013 with the work りり|Kagarigari}}. Kagarigari is a 45-page Demon-Slaying manga.

The next year, 2014, they published their debut in the Jump Next 2014 vol.2 issue, with a 45 page oneshot titled |Monju Shirō Kyōdai}}. Later that year, they created a new 46 page oneshot titled さん|Rokkotsu-san}}, published in Weekly Shonen Jump 2014-39 issue. The one-shot was part of Jump's Golden Future Cup as entry #3.

enrichments.description:
The |Mugen Ressha}} was an esteemed passenger train and the eponymous setting of the Mugen Train Arc. After 40 of its passengers went missing, the Demon Slayer Corps was sent to investigate the train.

The Mugen Train was a black steam-powered locomotive, specifically a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JGR_Class_8620# JGR Class 8620]. It has a plaque with the word Mugen (lit. "Infinity") on its smokebox door. It was a passenger train carrying eight dark-brown coaches.

Sometime after the Lower Ranks Meeting, several passengers of the Mugen Train went missing, with the casualty count reaching at least 40. This suspicious pattern was not lost on the Demon Slayer Corps, who suspected that a demon was behind the disappearances. Flame Hashira Kyojuro Rengoku was assigned to investigate the train, and with the recommendation of Insect Hashira Shinobu Kocho, Demon Slayers Tanjiro Kamado, Zenitsu Agatsuma, and Inosuke Hashibira were also sent to accompany him. However, only Zenitsu who had grew up in a urban area was familiar with the train, as Tanjiro mistook it for a forest spirit and Inosuke mistook it for a monster.

The Demon Slayer Corps received word that the train was secretly transported to a certain storage area after a conductor had been murdered. As Kyojuro personally visited the storage facility, he met train maintenance workers who were fixing the train despite the rumors that it had become a man-eater and informed him that it was scheduled to return to service tomorrow. Kyojuro suddenly encountered a murderous demon serial killer named the Slasher, but after dispatching him, he concluded that he was not the culprit responsible for the 40 casualties.

enrichments.description:
The Demon Slayer Corps is an organization dedicated to hunting and killing demons. Most members of the Demon Slayer Corps are combatants, known as Demon Slayers.

As the Demon Slayer Corps isn't officially recognized by the Japanese government, its members are forced to work in secrecy, which means that Demon Slayers cannot openly carry their swords in public. The majority of people are unaware of the existence of demons, and even if Demon Slayers were to reveal the truth about their job, they would be met with skepticism and disbelief from most individuals. Allowing Demon Slayers to openly wield swords would only incite chaos and confusion among the general population. By maintaining a low profile and avoid drawing unnecessary attention, they can carry out their duties covertly and effectively. Nevertheless, whispers of the Demon Slayers have permeated public consciousness, existing as mere folklore in the minds of some. However, when civilians encounter demons or witness a Demon Slayer engaging a demon firsthand, they come face-to-face with the reality of their existence and the truth behind the tales they've heard.

Without any support from the government or other sponsors, the Demon Slayer Corps relies solely on the resources provided by the Ubuyashiki family for its daily operations. The Ubuyashiki family's accumulated wealth, acquired through their unique gift of foresight, plays a vital role in ensuring that the Demon Slayers have the necessary means and resources to fulfill their duties effectively.

The Demon Slayer Corps was founded approximately a thousand years ago during the Heian Era. This occurred after Muzan Kibutsuji, a distant relative of the current Ubuyashiki Family, inadvertently became the very first demon. As a result, a curse befell the Ubuyashiki bloodline, causing subsequent generations to suffer from premature deaths. Seeking guidance, the Ubuyashiki family heeded the advice of a priest and established the Corps. They took on the responsibility of leading the battle against Muzan and his demons, believing that by eradicating demons from the world, they could break the curse that plagued their bloodline.

enrichments.description:
The |Hashira|lit. Pillars}} are the highest-ranking Demon Slayers in the Demon Slayer Corps.

Hashira is the highest rank that Demon Slayers can obtain in the Demon Slayer Corps. Those who hold the position are regarded as the most powerful and skilled combatants in the entire organization, protecting humanity against more dangerous threats that cannot be handled by other Demon Slayers.

The Hashira, in accordance with their great strength, hold the highest authority in the organization, second only to the Corps leader, Kagaya Ubuyashiki, and later, Kiriya Ubuyashiki.

The Hashira are all assigned a specific region that they are required to patrol, usually to gather information about the demons inhabiting said area and to improve their swordsmanship. They are also deployed on missions only if lower-ranking members are unable to complete it.

enrichments.description:
The |Jūnikizuki|lit. Twelve Demon Moons}} is an organization of the twelve most powerful demons who are under the direct command of the Demon King, Muzan Kibutsuji. They serve as the main antagonistic faction of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba.

The Twelve Kizuki is a body of the 12 strongest individuals amongst demon-kind, second in strength and authority only to the Demon King himself, Muzan. Each member of the Twelve Kizuki has received a large portion of Muzan's blood, greater than any other demon, thus exponentially increasing their power. As a testament to this, every member of the Twelve Kizuki can use Blood Demon Arts; supernatural powers and techniques manifested through their blood that only significantly powerful demons have access to.

The Twelve Kizuki are divided into two groups: the six |Jōgen}}, numbered one through six, and the six |Kagen}}, also numbered one through six. The number signifies their ranking among the Twelve Kizuki, determined by each member's level of strength, Upper Rank One being the strongest and Lower Rank Six being the weakest. The Lower Ranks have their numbers and ranks engraved only into one eye, whereas the Upper Ranks have their numbers in one eye and the kanji for |Jōgen}} in the other.

While the exact relationships between the two groups are unclear, it is known that the Upper Ranks despise the Lower Ranks. The Upper Ranks each possess a level of power that far surpasses that of the Lower Ranks; as proof of their strength, the strongest of the Demon Slayer Corps, the Hashira, have killed numerous Lower Ranks over the years, while the Upper Ranks have killed and eaten many Hashira over the years. Kagaya Ubuyashiki states that it had been over a hundred years since an Upper Rank has been killed following the defeat of Gyutaro and Daki. Furthermore, it has been remarked by Shinobu Kocho that the strength of an Upper Rank demon is, at least at minimum, comparable to three Hashira, although it should be noted that the capabilities of a Hashira vary from one to another, especially the ones who can manifest their Demon Slayer Marks to further augment their strength. While the Lower Ranks have been replaced countless times, the Upper Ranks have not changed over the past 100 years at all, as a testament to the strength of its members.

enrichments.description:
The Infinity Castle is a pocket dimension consisting of lamplit wooden rooms, long halls, and moving corridors. It possesses a warped direction of gravity, allowing demons to stand upright, upside down, perpendicularly on the walls, or move in physically impossible directions. Its unusual structure and layout is controlled by Nakime's Blood Demon Art, allowing any structure within to shift at her will, though the castle additionally seems to move on its own.

Using her biwa, she can manipulate the position of any demon inside and take them to any location in her range. During the conclusion of the Lower Ranks Meeting, Nakime teleported Muzan to a balcony leading outside despite his original position being deep within the castle; Morever, the doors she used to close around him all seem to constantly shift within the unusual gravity, spinning within themselves as she changes its layout.

The Infinity Castle's range seems to extend beyond its already incomprehensibly large area, as Nakime was able to manipulate Enmu and take him to an unknown town seemingly nowhere close to the castle, even dropping him in place using a supernatural vanishing door. She was also able to transport Gyokko and Hantengu from the Infinity Castle to the Swordsmith Village after Muzan ordered them on a mission there. During the Hashira's initial confrontation with Muzan, upon seeing them close in on him, Muzan gave Nakime the signal to open doors that caused them to fall into the castle, despite their initial location being in the extremely well-hidden Ubuyashiki Mansion. The location of the castle at that moment is transported to an area deep under the ground of a city, far away from where the Ubuyashikis predicted they would be.

Only certain demons seem to be aware of the Infinity Castle's existence, as Akaza did not have any difficulty traversing across the dimension, making use of its unusual gravity and shifting rooms to make his way across, whereas the Lower Ranks during their gathering with Muzan were completely out of their element; when Wakuraba attempted to escape Muzan attempting to kill him, no matter how far and how quickly he ran, he remained trapped within the same area of the Infinity Castle. However, since Nezuko Kamado's immunity to sunlight was revealed, lesser demons have been seen gathering in large numbers in the Infinity Castle.

Nichirin swords (among other Nichirin bladed weapons) are the main weapons used by Demon Slayers in the Demon Slayer Corps in order to kill demons. They are forged from |Shōjōhi Satetsu}} and |Shōjōhi Kōseki}}, both of which are found on high mountains like the Sunlight Mountain, which is perpetually bathed in sunlight all throughout the year on |Yōkōsan|}}.

As they constantly absorb sunlight, decapitating demons with Nichirin swords can permanently kill them. Once their neck-bone is slashed by the weapon, their heads and bodies disintegrate into ash in a similar fashion to when exposed to sunlight. However, despite their sunlight-absorbent properties, Nichirin swords are less effective when used to slash other parts of a demon's body, making beheading the only viable option for Demon Slayers.

Nichirin swords take on a distinct color when first drawn by its owner, which is why they are also referred to as "Color Changing Katanas". However, the holder is required to have a certain amount of skill, or the blade will not change color.

Demon Slayer recruits choose their own ore after successfully passing Final Selection. The ore will then be used by a swordsmith of the Swordsmith Village for the forging process of a Nichirin sword, and the swordsmith will personally bring the weapon to the Demon Slayer.

enrichments.description:
Breathing Styles are swordsmanship styles that makes use of an esoteric breathing technique known as Total Concentration Breathing, and are practiced and taught by members of the Demon Slayer Corps to be used in combat (later passed on as traditional dances post-time skip).

All known Breathing Styles currently taught within the Demon Slayer Corps are derived from Sun Breathing, the first one ever created. The majority of known Breathing Styles mimic a certain element of nature (i.e. flame, water and wind) and replicates it with the user's movements, techniques and abilities. The weapon attacks of Demon Slayers who use Breathing Styles are also longer ranged, possibly due to shockwaves or air pressure generated from their weapon itself when swinging and striking.

New Breathing Styles are always being created to suit a Demon Slayer's combat needs, which results in new weapons being utilized in demon hunting (i.e. flails and whips). Such Breathing Styles embody a bigger variety of concepts, like animals, plants and emotions (i.e. serpents, flowers and love). In any case, these new creations always branch out of the five fundamental Breathing Styles. Many of them are personal creations limited to only one user due to a trait or combat style unique to them, but there are cases when branching Breathing Styles have found usage from other Demon Slayers aside from their creators. In both cases, the users are Hashira-level Demon Slayers or at least highly-skilled and competent. When utilizing a Breathing Style, users automatically visualize themselves manipulating the concept behind their style, making it seem as if they were using magic, though those that are less apt and proficient in their style will visualize less of it than one who is.

It's possible to blend different Breathing Styles when mastering a single one proves challenging. Tanjiro Kamado, for instance, couldn't fully master Water Breathing like Giyu Tomioka or handle the strain of Hinokami Kagura, so he combined these styles to harness their strengths. This fusion allowed him to deliver more powerful strikes and sustain longer battles, as demonstrated when he rescued Hinatsuru from Gyutaro. Tanjiro later employed this hybrid style again during the Infinity Castle Arc, where he effectively dispatched numerous demons.

enrichments.description:
Water Breathing is a Breathing Style that mimics water, specifically the flow, flexibility and adaptability of the liquid and replicates it with the user's movements, techniques and abilities. Most, if not all, known techniques involve the user bending their body, arm and weapon in a fluid motion to match the movements of rushing or flowing water. Users also visualize themselves seemingly creating and manipulating water when unleashing its techniques.

This Breathing Style was originally created by one of Yoriichi Tsugikuni's students who attempted to learn Sun Breathing, but due to not being as innately talented as Yoriichi, he was instead taught and trained an alternative personalized Breathing Style that focused on his strengths and weaknesses, eventually becoming Water Breathing.

It is said to be the most common Breathing Style among Demon Slayers due to being the easiest to learn for beginners. A known Cultivator of Water Breathing in the Demon Slayer Corps is Sakonji Urokodaki, though there are other Cultivators as well.

enrichments.description:
The Hinokami Kagura is a Breathing Style that is passed on from father to son in every generation of Kamado Family alongside the Hanafuda-like earrings. They use it within a ritual ceremony practiced every new year, where the Breathing Style user offers the Fire God a dance from sunset to sunrise to ward off threats and diseases.

The dance is composed of twelve segments repeated throughout the night until dawn. Tanjuro Kamado noted that the breathing technique utilized in this dance allows the user to never exhaust themselves no matter how long they move, making it such that they can seemingly dance forever. The last user of Hinokami Kagura as a swordsman technique is Tanjiro Kamado, who learned the Breathing Style from his father Tanjuro Kamado, and would utilize it to fight various demons.

The Hinokami Kagura is later revealed by Shinjuro Rengoku to be a legendary Breathing Style known as の|Hi no Kokyū}}, the first one to have ever been created, though it was seemingly lost. All other Breathing Styles are derived from it as the result of Yoriichi Tsugikuni, its creator, modifying it to suit the individuals he taught who were unable to use it.

Both the Hinokami Kagura and Sun Breathing are Breathing Styles that mimic the sun and replicate it with the user's movements, techniques, and abilities. All techniques and forms are extremely varied and have no set pattern, making it the most versatile and effective against demons. Users of Sun Breathing visualize themselves seemingly manipulating solar flames when unleashing its techniques.

Thunder Breathing is a Breathing Style that mimics and replicates lightning based attacks/movements, specifically swift strikes and movements akin to lightning ripping through the sky, and replicates it with the user's movements, techniques and abilities. Most, if not all, known techniques and forms involve utilizing blinding speeds and immensely fast attacks to overwhelm the enemy in an instant. Users of Thunder Breathing also visualize themselves seemingly creating and manipulating lightning and electricity when unleashing its techniques.

It has been remarked by Zenitsu Agatsuma that this Breathing Style focuses on channeling strength into the user's legs, and maximizing the output of every single muscle and blood vessel in them. Users also mimic lightning to such high fidelity that they cause the air to vibrate when poised to unleash a technique and create immensely loud sounds akin to thunder with their mere footsteps. This Breathing Style is also very reminiscent of a swordsmanship style practiced and utilized in real life known as Iaijutsu, a famous quick-draw sword technique.

This Breathing Style was created by one of Yoriichi Tsugikuni's students who attempted to learn Sun Breathing. But due to not being as innately powerful as Yoriichi, he was instead taught an alternated personalized Breathing Style that focused on their individual strengths and weaknesses, which eventually evolved into Thunder Breathing.

A known Cultivator of Thunder Breathing in the Demon Slayer Corps is the former Rumble Hashira, Jigoro Kuwajima.

enrichments.description:
Before he became a Demon Slayer, Tanjiro was a coal burner until his family was attacked by Muzan, leaving his mother and younger siblings dead, and Nezuko transformed into a demon.

Tanjiro is a young man of average height with lightly tanned skin and an athletic, muscular build. His hair is ruffled and black with red tips (appearing black that turns to burgundy at the tips in the anime), and is swept back to reveal his forehead. His eyes are wide and dark red, fading into a burgundy hue with white pupils that appear lighter toward the lower section of the iris, while the upper portion is markedly darker. He bears a distinct scar on the upper left of his forehead, first seen when his mother took him to watch his father perform the Hinokami Kagura dance. Originally, it was a light pink, patch-like mark — an injury he received after saving one of his siblings from a hot brazier. It remained so until his battle with the Hand Demon during Final Selection, after which it developed into a dark red, jagged mark. Later, during Hashira Training, it transformed once more into a true, permanent flame-like pattern — his Demon Slayer Mark. It is also noted that Tanjiro’s hands are unusually rough for someone his age, a testament to the grueling training he endured under Sakonji Urokodaki. In appearance, Tanjiro closely resembles his ancestor Sumiyoshi, sharing the same facial features, eyes, and hairstyle. However, Sumiyoshi’s hair was longer - reaching shoulder-length, and tied back into a ponytail.

Tanjiro first appears wearing a checkered, black-and-biscay-green haori over a white robe and black pants. He occasionally sports a turquoise scarf and is seen with circular white bands looped around his calves. He also wears a distinct pair of hanafuda-like earrings with the image of the rising, red sun over a mountain. His hair is also kept tied back in a small ponytail or bun; as he trains with Sabito and Makomo, his hair grows to his shoulders.

During Final Selection, Tanjiro wears a blue, cloud-patterned samue-styled kimono and black pants, nearly identical to Sakonji's outfit. He still wears his earrings, but his hair is cut extremely short and has remained the same length since. Similar to the rest of the apprentices that were trained under Sakonji, Tanjiro wears a hand-carved fox mask crafted by his master on the left side of his head. The mask has red accents on the eyes, ears, and spots on each corner of its mouth. On the upper right corner of the mask, there is a sun-shaped design that likely symbolizes the scar on his forehead.

enrichments.description:
Nezuko is a young girl with fair skin, visibly large prominent fangs, a slender build, and sharp stiletto nails with a base color of light pink and ombre transitioning to a red-orange color at the tips. Her hair is long, black, and wavy. It reaches just below her waist, turning a flame-orange color as it passes her elbows, and appears to be crimped into large straight ridges, worn side-swept drastically to her left. She has soft-looking pink pupils that appear a lighter color around the rims of their irises and a persian pink center; they slanted downwards toward the sides of her face and framed by notably long eyelashes. In the manga, Nezuko can sometimes be shown with more than one bow. According to Tanjiro, Nezuko was known as a great beauty in their home town.

She wears a light pink, short-sleeve kimono with an asanoha (hemp leaf) pattern, the lining a paler pink layered with the white wavy yuban underneath as a medium-length trailing skirt kimono to freely move as a demon; this, the white clothes lowly cover her knees then goes down to almost her ankles making a open window, secured by a red and white-chequered hanhaba obi with an orange-threaded obijime and a green obiage. Over this, she sports a long dark-brown haori that reaches her calves, as well as a pair of zōri with pink straps and white tabi socks, wrapped with thick pieces of black material resembling kyahan. Nezuko also wears a small pink ribbon on the left side of her head to keep her hair out of her face, along with the bamboo muzzle Giyu Tomioka gave her, which is secured around her jaw with a strip of red cloth.

When Nezuko transforms into her awakened form during her fight with Daki, she gains a bigger, taller, and more curvaceous body. As a result, she outgrows her attire, tearing the sleeves of her kimono and the left sleeve of her haori. In addition, she loses her bamboo muzzle and her right footwear. She grows a short white horn on the right side of her forehead, designed with an irregular crack pattern, along with vein-like patterns in her forehead near her horn. She has a vein-like pattern around her left eye. In addtion, she has black cat-like slit pupils, along with crack-like patterns around the rim of her irises. Her most striking new feature is the red and green vine-like pattern that covers her skin, circling around her arms, legs, and chest.

After gaining immunity from sunlight and regaining her ability to speak, Nezuko retains mostly the same appearance. Exceptions include the removal of her bamboo muzzle and her eyes, which now have black, cat-like pupils with visible cracks.

enrichments.description:
Zenitsu is a young man of average height, fair skin, and muscular build. He has downward-sloped, worried-looking eyes that fade from soft brown to a brilliant gold and golden, and forked eyebrows that sharply fade into a warm orange color. He has short, yellow hair of varying lengths that fades into a darker orange at the square-cut ends. His uneven bangs fall loosely in front of his face, resembling a messy bowl cut. Before he became a Demon Slayer, Zenitsu's hair was originally black, but it turned the color it is currently when he was struck by lightning during his training.

For some time following the battle at Mount Natagumo, his limbs temporarily shrank to Son's poison but were able to return to normal afterward thanks to the medicine developed by Shinobu Kocho.

Zenitsu wears a golden brown variation of the standard Demon Slayer uniform, which consists of a button-up jacket with a stand-up collar and long sleeves. The outfit features silver buttons and a shirt pocket on the left breast. Additionally, the kanji for |Metsu}} is engraved on the back of the uniform. Underneath the jacket, he wears a white long-sleeved collared undershirt. A white belt is tied around his waist, securing a pair of matching golden brown tattsuke-hakama pants that are wrapped at the calves with his distinctive, bright yellow-to-orange gradient kyahan. These kyahan are tied in the front with three white bows and bear the same white-triangle pattern as his haori. Zenitsu also wears golden brown tabi socks and a pair of white zōri sandals with white straps. Over his uniform, he sports his signature haori, a bright yellow-to-orange gradient decorated with a repeating white triangle pattern.

As an adult, although he drew himself as a tall and sleek man with a prominent moustache, he actually had a plump and puffy figure and grew little facial hair.

A millennium ago during the Heian period, Muzan was turned into a demon from an experimental treatment for his terminal illness he's had since birth and his goal ever since then has been to live without the fear of death and become truly eternal. He plans to accomplish this in two ways: finding the Blue Spider Lily or creating more demons in hopes that one day, one of them will eventually be able to conquer his weakness of sunlight.

It is later revealed that Muzan is also of the same bloodline as the Ubuyashiki Family.

Muzan is a tall man with a lean, muscular build alongside an unnaturally pale skin complexion that can be easily confused with being unhealthy and sickly. He has parted, short-length and wavy black hair, with two sets of bangs on each side of his face in the middle. He has sharp, almond-shaped eyes with vibrant red irises and black, vertical, cat-like pupils, which are surrounded by visible cracks. He also possesses sharp, blue nails that fades into a light blue color at the tip. Physically, he appears to be in his twenties.

During the Heian period, Muzan's appearance as a human wasn't very different from his current look, only lacking his fangs and slit pupils. Interestingly, a model sheet revealed that his eyes were still a red color. Muzan wore a sokutai outfit, with a black robe highlighted with gray patterns and a kanmuri headwear. When he grew increasingly sickly, Muzan then wore a plain white kimono, long hair, and had visible eye bags.

Kyojuro was a young man of tall stature and lean-muscular build, with fair skin. He had long, somewhat messy and bright yellow hair that flared out around his face, with red streaks akin to flames along with two shoulder-length bangs, two chin-length bangs on the side of his head, and wore a messily ponytail behind his head. He had black forked eyebrows and golden eyes that turns to red around the irises with white pupils. He was known to be charismatic and had an air of great optimism, having an enthusiastic smile plastered on his face nearly all the time.

Kyojuro wore the standard Demon Slayer Corps uniform, which is black in the manga and tinted a deep brown in the anime. It consisted of a brown button-up jacket with a stand-up collar and long sleeves, featuring gold buttons and a shirt pocket on the left breast, with the kanji for |Metsu}} engraved on the back of the uniform. Beneath the jacket, he wore a white long-sleeved collared undershirt. His uniform was fastened with a white belt at the waist and included traditional tattsuke-hakama pants of matching color. Over this, Kyojuro wore a striking haori draped on his shoulders like a cape, with a white-to-yellow gradient pattern and red flame-like ridges at the end. This haori originally belonged to his father, Shinjuro Rengoku, and was more than likely worn by him when he served as the Flame Hashira before Kyojuro inherited the role. For legwear, he wore a pair of red kyahan decorated with yellow flame motifs rising from the bottom up, brown tabi socks, and a pair of white zōri sandals with red straps.

When Kyojuro first joined the Demon Slayer Corps, he wore the regular Demon Slayer uniform paired with a plain white haori. His outfit remained the same as he rose up the ranks, before finally donning the iconic flame-patterned haori following his ascension to Hashira.

Shinobu was a petite, young woman of slender build. Her complexion was notably pale, contrasting with the pink of her lips. She had large, pupil-less eyes that resembled those of insects. Her irises featured a hazy purple gradient that darkened toward the bottom, accented by white highlights at the top. Her eyes were framed with thick eyelashes. She had hair that was raven-black, fading into a purple hue at the ends. Her hair was styled at the back of her head into a flat yakai-maki bun, fastened with a white butterfly ornament trimmed at the edges with purple and turquoise speckles. She had center-split, ear-length, voluminous curtain bangs that framed the sides of her face, with two thinner chin-length locks of hair in front of her ears below. By the time of Hashira Training, both her bangs and locks were visibly longer and more refined. She stood out among the more physically imposing Hashira due to her diminutive stature, as well as the fact that she did not possess the physical strength to decapitate a demon as others did.

Shinobu wore a dark purple-tinted variation of the standard Demon Slayer uniform. It consisted of a button-up jacket with a stand-up collar and long sleeves. The uniform featured gold buttons and a shirt pocket on the left breast, with the kanji for |Metsu}} engraved on the back. Beneath the jacket, she wore a white long-sleeved collared undershirt. Her long, saggy tattsuke-hakama pants were tinted dark purple and were fastened at the waist with a white belt. Her legs were wrapped with a pair of white kyahan—with butterfly-patterned design—that transitioned from pale turquoise to pink gradient around the lower legs, tied securely with white ribbons. Her tabi socks matched the color of her uniform.

Over her uniform, she wore a distinctive haori that once belonged to her late older sister, Kanae. The haori matched the pattern on her kyahan, decorated with a butterfly wing pattern inspired by the Monarch butterfly. Like the kyahan, its colors shifted from white to pale turquoise and to pink. The cuffs and hem had a black trim decorated with pale turquoise dots. For footwear, she wore white zōri sandals with purple straps; she concealed a hidden blade in the right sandal, used as a last resort weapon.

When Shinobu was fourteen, her appearance was slightly different. Her chin-length strands of hair in front of her ears were tucked in and she had a different Demon Slayer uniform consisting of silver buttons, with the cloth a darker shade of purple. She also sported a plain white haori.

Tengen is a very tall, broad-shouldered, and incredibly muscular man with lightly-tanned skin and white hair. His hair is of an uneven length, the longest strands reaching his shoulders, and is styled with three more notable, shorter clumps arching up to fall as bangs between his eyes and on either side of his face. He has thin, dark fuchsia eyes that appear to slant inwards, each with one long eyelash flowing to the far side of his face. He also painted his fingernails and toenails with claret and bright green color. He is considered very attractive as noted by many women and even by Zenitsu; this has led him to use his looks as a tool for his missions whenever persuasion is necessary.

During his service as the Sound Hashira of the Demon Slayer Corps, Tengen wore a highly customized, sleeveless version of the standard Demon Slayer uniform. His uniform was black in the manga and tinted a deep dark turquoise in the anime. It consisted of a sleeveless button-up jacket with a stand-up collar, gold buttons, and a shirt pocket on the left breast, with the kanji for |Metsu}} engraved on the back of the uniform. Underneath, he wore a white sleeveless collared undershirt. The uniform was secured with a white belt at the waist and included matching tattsuke-hakama pants tucked into burgundy cloth wrappings around his calves. On his feet, he wore white zōri sandals with white straps and dark turquoise [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabi tabi socks] to match his uniform. Tengen is accessorized flamboyantly, wearing two thick, golden rings around his upper arms and a pair of fingerless purple gloves. These gloves were secured with two silver bands around the middle fingers and fastened at the wrists with two thinner golden rings on each side.

As well as this, Tengen sports a white head-wrap that covers his hair, leaving only a thin ponytail visible to fall behind his head from between its layers. Adorning his forehead was a striking pale gray headband, embellished with six pale pink gemstones—three large ones arranged in a horizontal row across the center, and three smaller ones arranged in a triangular formation on the far left side. From each side of this headdress hung chains of smaller pale blue gemstones, which framed his face like earrings or decorative tassels. Additionally, Tengen wore distinctive red eye makeup on his left eye, composed of alternating large and small dots that extended inward toward the corner of his eye. He also wears a pair of two golden cuff earrings on each ears.

After his retirement from the Demon Slayer Corps due to the injuries he has sustained during his fight with Gyutaro, Tengen changes his appearance to coordinate the loss of his left eye and hand. He now wears a long, burgundy colored yukata with white yuban collar along a light purple obi tied around the waist, and an indigo blue haori. He also replaces his old head-wrap with a dark eyepatch adorned with what look to be the remaining gemstones left over from his old headdress, leaving his hair to fall loosely past his shoulders. In addition, a long scar from where Gyutaro's kama sliced his left eye is visible under his eyepatch. He also wears a pair of zōri.

Sakonji is a reasonably tall elderly man with fair skin tone, as noted by the countless number of students he has trained, along with his silver-colored hair. His face has never once been revealed or depicted throughout the entire completed manga; he is always seen wearing a tengu mask that covers his entire face although Tanjiro states through a Taisho Secret that Sakonji's face is very gentle and calm.

He is always seen wearing a blue, cloud-patterned jinbei kimono with navy colored pants which are fastened at his shins by white kyahan guards. He also wears traditional black tabi socks, and sandals similar to Tanjiro, except his sandals have blue straps. On the occasions when Sakonji travels, he wears a white cloth that covers his head and wraps around his neck.

When he was younger, his hair was black and fashioned into a topknot.

As a trainer and former Demon Slayer, Sakonji is pragmatic, strict, and vigilant, while simultaneously sympathetic and understanding. When first meeting Tanjiro, he was quick to criticize him for his weak resolve and innate kindness, harshly telling him the solution to when Nezuko eats someone is to kill her and then himself. He possessed a no-nonsense demeanour while training Tanjiro, repeatedly kicking, beating, and harshly instructing him to get his bearings together and get things quickly and properly; he even began to utilize traps armed with knives and spikes when Tanjiro began to improve his descent of his mountain. That said, he became incredibly proud of the Demon Slayer Tanjiro would become.

Sanemi is also the older brother of Genya Shinazugawa, a Demon Slayer who fought alongside Tanjiro Kamado and Nezuko Kamado.

Sanemi is a tall, very muscular young man with a light skin tone, and long, spiky, ruffled silver-white hair, featuring two large bangs on the left and middle side of his face, which he cuts short some time between the events of the Hashira meeting and the Mugen train incident. He has large almond-shaped eyes, long eyelashes. and small, pale purple irises with dark swirls, which turn bloodshot whenever he's angry. He also has dark patches beneath his eyes, making him appear perpetually tired or restless, giving him a crazed expression on his face.

Sanemi's appearance is notable for his many scars. A large, jagged scar runs across the upper right side of his forehead toward the center, accompanied by an X-shaped scar that cuts across his right temple and extends down through his right brow, lying just beneath the first. Another prominent, uneven scar goes over his right cheekbone and across the bridge of his nose — which came from an injury he sustained as a child when his transformed mother attacked him. He has another X-shaped scar on his chest, and a large, diagonal scar across his abdomen. He has four smaller scars on both his hands and forearms, which he sustained from past battles with demons.

Ufotable, Inc. (Japanese: ユーフォーテーブル有限会社, Hepburn: Yūfōtēburu yūgen-gaisha) is a Japanese animation studio founded in October 2000 by former Telecom Animation Film producer Hikaru Kondō and located in Shinjuku, Tokyo.

A hallmark seen in many of their works (Ninja Nonsense, Futakoi Alternative, Coyote Ragtime Show, Gakuen Utopia Manabi Straight!, Tales of Symphonia, The Garden of Sinners) is a claymation sequence.

They have had a long relationship with Type-Moon, having produced adaptations of their works such as Fate/Zero, Fate/stay night: Unlimited Blade Works, and The Garden of Sinners, as well as Bandai Namco Entertainment, for whom they have produced an opening animation and cutscenes for many of their games, primarily in the Tales and God Eater series.

In 2025, the studio produced the highest-grossing anime film of all time, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – The Movie: Infinity Castle. The film surpassed the studio's previous record-holder, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – The Movie: Mugen Train (2020), which was the first non-Hollywood production to top the annual global box office.

enrichments.description:
A demon is an evil or malevolent supernatural entity, though they can be benevolent too. Historically, belief in demons, or stories about demons, occurs in folklore, mythology, religion, occultism, and literature; these beliefs are reflected in media including fiction, comics, film, television, and video games. Belief in demons probably goes back to the Paleolithic age, stemming from humanity's fear of the unknown, the strange and the horrific. In ancient Near Eastern religions and in the Abrahamic religions, including early Judaism and ancient-medieval Christian demonology, a demon is considered a harmful spiritual entity that may cause demonic possession, calling for an exorcism. Large portions of Jewish demonology, a key influence on Christianity and Islam, originated from a later form of Zoroastrianism, and was transferred to Judaism during the Persian era.

Demons may or may not be considered to be devils: minions of the Devil. In many traditions, demons are independent operators, with different demons causing different types of evils (destructive natural phenomena, specific diseases, etc.) in general, while devils appear more often as demons within a theological framework; demons opposing the Divine principle. As lesser spirits doing the Devil's work, they have additional duties—causing humans to have sinful thoughts and tempting humans to commit sinful actions.

The original Ancient Greek word daimōn (δαίμων) did not carry negative connotations, as it denotes a spirit or divine power. The Greek conception of a daimōn notably appears in the philosophical works of Plato, where it describes the divine inspiration of Socrates. In Christianity, morally ambivalent daimōn were replaced by demons, forces of evil only striving for corruption. Such demons are not the Greek intermediary spirits, but hostile entities, already known in Iranian beliefs. In Western esotericism and Renaissance magic, which grew out of an amalgamation of Greco-Roman magic, Jewish Aggadah, and Christian demonology, a demon is believed to be a spiritual entity that may be conjured and controlled.

Belief in demons remains an important part of many modern religions and occult traditions. Demons are still feared largely due to their alleged power to possess living creatures. Within a psychological context demons may be used as metaphors for inner psychological processes ("inner demons").

entities.name: Akeno Tsugikuni
entities.description:
Akeno was a young woman with a petite build and fair skin. She has black waist-length hair tied parted apart on top of her forehead with a bow at the bottom of her back along with two bangs that reach her eyes.

She wore a magenta kimono with a white juban under it. Over this, Akeno wore incredibly long formal clothing that could possibly be or inspired by Jūnihitoe with multiple thin overlapping white crescent moons with polka-dots above them, reaching past her bare feet being dragged along the floor.

Akeno was described as a very religious and pure-hearted woman, always praying to the god of the sun for little to no disaster in the world along with her constantly worrying for Yoriichi and Michikatsu. She was noted to be a very calm and quiet person, with people describing her demeanour as doll-like. Despite this, she also possesses a fierce love for her children, as shown when she accosts her husband for considering killing Yoriichi. Despite her protective constitution, she doesn't complain to being helped as seen when Yoriichi as a child would always support and carry her impaired side due to her terminal sickness.

Akeno lived during the Sengoku period of Japan, nearly five centuries before the Taisho era. She gave birth to twin boys in a time it was thought to be a bad omen, as twins would have fought to be the family's rightful heir. In particular, the younger twin had a large and strange looking mark on the upper-left side of his head. This caused her husband to consider killing the boy just after his birth. At this, Akeno became furious and angrily grabbed her husband's haori, needing to be restrained by two servants. She vouched for his survival and he eventually relented, deciding the boy would live in the temples when old enough. Of her two boys, the older one was named Michikatsu and the younger twin was named Yoriichi.

entities.name: Akito Ubuyashiki
entities.description:
As a child, Akito greatly resembled his posthumous nephew Kiriya, having a black bobcut adorned with a wisteria headpiece. He also wore a floral print kimono with the exact same design as his [https://kimetsu-no-yaiba.fandom.com/wiki/Kuina_Ubuyashiki nieces], and a striped obi with a circular design, supported with a obiage and obijime. Akito was seen with a gentle, if not reserved and passive expression.

Unlike the kind and understanding Kagaya or resentful and dour Senri, Akito appeared to be meek, quiet, and compliant. Due to his brother convincing him to set their home ablaze, Akito seemed to be unable to stand up to himself and carried out Senri's instructions without question, leading to his death.

Akito was the youngest child of his generation of the Ubuyashiki family. His elder brother Senri, who resented his illness and his father's suicide as a result of his position as Oyakata, forced Akito to set fire to the mansion, as well as joining him to commit double-suicide. Their mother would die from the fire in an attempt to save them, leaving Kagaya as the sole survivor.

entities.name: Amane Ubuyashiki
entities.description:
Amane was a woman of average height and pale skin complexion in contrast with her red lips. She possessed large, plum purple eyes (with pink eyeshadow) and short eyebrows, a trait seen in her children. She wore her white hair down and swept to both the left and right at the front and in a short ponytail in the back, with two strands of hair loose at the side of her head. Her beauty was apparent as Muichiro Tokito once described her as appearing like a forest spirit when they first met, and Mitsuri Kanroji, being asked to speak by Amane, took the chance to admire her beauty.

Amane wore a salmon-colored kimono with an ombre to orange at the top with flower patterns with a dark-indigo haori with numerous blue butterfly-patterns. She also wore a brown with a paler shade striped-obi with an orange obiage supporting it.

Amane was shown to possess the same quiet, strict and serious disposition as her husband and children, acting professionally and tactfully when communicating with the Hashira during her time filling in for husband when his health began to fail. She was shown to be just as devoted to the Demon Slayer Corps as her husband and children as well, and spared no time in trying to figure out anything that could be used to turn the tide of battle in to their favor.

As well as this, Amane has been shown to truly love and care for her husband, Kagaya Ubuyashiki, and is seen constantly nursing him and staying by his side as his body slowly began to fail and his health further worsened. In fact, the only time Amane dropped her usual controlled demeanor was when Kagaya's health began to severely plummet and he began to cough out blood, causing her to immediately panic and worry as she barked out orders for her children to help her treat him, showing a genuine sense of love between them. During a moment alone with him, Kagaya held her hand and thanked her for everything she has done, causing her to quietly cry and return his sentiment.

entities.name: Aoba Hashibira
entities.description:
Aoba shares a striking resemblance with his ancestor, having feminine features that cause people to mistake him for a woman. He has black, shoulder length hair with overlapping bangs and emerald green eyes. However, unlike Inosuke, Aoba has a physically smaller build and jet black hair rather than hair that fades from black to blue like Inosuke's, the same as Aoi.

As a researcher, he wears a standard uniform consisting of a white button up shirt and lab coat, as well as blue slacks and black shoes.

Unlike either of his ancestors, Inosuke and Aoi, Aoba was soft-spoken and timid. Being the leading researcher in charge of study the Blue Spider Lily, he held a press conference to apologize to the public for a mistake in their research and took it upon himself to shoulder the blame, showing that he was earnest and sincere.

Despite their stark contrast in character, Aoba has shown one similarity to Inosuke. Following the mistake in his study, he had voiced his wish to "live alone deep in the mountains", following the backlash he endured.

entities.name: Aoi Kanzaki
entities.description:
Aoi is a young woman of average height and pale skin complexion. She has large, deep blue eyes that fade to a lighter blue at the bottom, along with white rectangular pupils. She has straight black hair with a parted fringe and twin-tails. She has dark, thin, and arched eyebrows which are usually furrowed due to the frown that she often has on her face. She wears two white butterfly ornaments that keeps her twin-tails in place. They have a light indigo-colored trim on the outer side of the wings, and are decorated with light turquoise-colored speckled spots.

Aoi wears the standard Demon Slayer uniform with the addition of a white nurse dress on top of it, with a blue sash around her waist. Her uniform is tinted slightly blue, along with pair of zōri with blue straps and white tabi socks. The uniform consisted of a button-up jacket with a stand-up collar and long sleeves, featuring silver buttons, a shirt pocket on the left breast, and the kanji for |Metsu}} engraved on the back of the uniform. Beneath the jacket, she wore a white long-sleeved collared undershirt, and her outfit was fastened at the waist with the standard white belt. She wore traditional tattsuke-hakama pants matching the blue color tone of her uniform.

Aoi is tough, uncompromising, strict, and serious, displaying an efficient and no-nonsensical attitude nearly at all times. While performing her duties in the Butterfly Mansion, she is effective and proactive, evident when she quickly demands a complaining Zenitsu to silence himself and take his medication; going so far as to demand he does not complain to her when he does not heal, despite his reluctance due to its bad taste.

Aoi's personality is somewhat similar to that of a younger Shinobu Kocho, being loud, volatile, and open. She often appears angry, generally displaying how she feels very clearly. However, she does occasionally express more tender emotions such as declaring her enjoyment of the time spent with the trio when they were at the Mansion, looking openly surprised at Tanjiro's reassurance towards her, and bursting into tears when discussing Inosuke's serious injuries.

entities.name: Asakusa Demon
entities.description:
The Asakusa Demon is a minor character in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba. He was a pedestrian in Asakusa who Muzan Kibutsuji turned into a demon.

The Asakusa Demon was once a man with ordinary features: average height, fair skin, short black hair, and black eyes. He wore a gray-green haori over a deep indigo kimono and a grey hakama. After being turned into a demon, his irises turned dark red with a white glow around his reduced pupils.

After being treated by Tamayo, the man no longer possesses his dark red eyes and fangs, and is now virtually indistinguishable from ordinary people.

One evening, as the man strolled with his wife along a bustling street in the vibrant city of Asakusa, they unknowingly walk pass by Muzan, Rei and their daughter. Muzan reaches behind and quickly scratches the man's neck with his sharp nails. Tanjiro Kamado is the only person witnessing the incident. Blood immediately spews from three deep gashes in the man's neck. He stops walking and grabs his neck in pain. Seeing him pause, his wife asks him what is wrong, but the man keeps his head down while Muzan's blood starts spreading through his veins. Gritting his teeth, the man then turns into a demon.

entities.name: Chachamaru
entities.description:
Chachamaru is a small, tricolor calico cat with a white base accompanied by black and brown spots. It has big amber eyes. On its back, it wears a brown box with a syringe created by Tamayo with the purpose of collecting demons' blood. Around its neck, it wears a red necklace with a paper talisman that was made and given by Yushiro, which it uses to hide with Yushiro's Blood Demon Art.

No information is given on the cat, it is simply introduced as Tamayo's feline familiar used as a transport mechanism for her medical studies. It can be presumed that it has been helping Tamayo and Yushiro for quite some time, as it is well-trained. Like many cats, Chachamaru likes pets, and will briefly stop for them before returning to its work.

In preparation for the final battle, Tamayo managed to transform Chachamaru into a demon, an act that weighed heavily on her heart. Despite Chachamaru having no agency or decision in the matter, Tamayo's primary concern was ensuring that Yushiro would not be left in solitude and consumed by loneliness. Interestingly, Chachamaru's own sentiments revealed a content acceptance of the transformation, driven by its unwavering love for Tamayo. No specific details are given regarding the process of its transformation.

Chachamaru first appears after Tanjiro's battle with former Lower Moon Six Kyogai. Initially it arrives invisibly until it meows and is revealed to Tanjiro. Tanjiro remembers the mission Tamayo gave to him and takes the blood of Kyogai using a needle. Once the blood-filled needle is tucked into the box on its back, Chachamaru hops away and becomes invisible once again to avoid detection.

entities.name: Chuntaro
entities.description:
Chuntaro is a small sparrow with brown eyes and reddish brown plumage that is mostly white, in addition to a few black feathers on his face.

Chuntaro is a very intelligent sparrow, as well as brave and loyal, as he is often seen trying to motivate Zenitsu to keep going when he feels down, or staying by his side in high-risk situations, such as when he entered and stayed with him on Mount Natagumo, despite all the discomfort that Zenitsu constantly causes him.

Chuntaro has also been shown to be very sentimental, such as when he was seen happy after Tanjiro understood him and agreed to help him the first time they met, or when, after the battle with the Spider Demon, Chuntaro stood next to Zenitsu with tearful eyes.

Chuntaro passed the Kasugai Crow Test after his family was killed by demons. He would later be assigned as Zenitsu Agatsuma's crow after he passed the Final Selection to become Demon Slayer.

entities.description:
Over a century ago during the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edo_period#:~:text=The%20Edo%20period%2C%20also%20known,regional%20daimyo%2C%20or%20feudal%20lords. Edo period], Daki was a human child by the name of |Ume}}, who lived in the Rashomon Riverbank of Yoshiwara, the lowest class of the Entertainment District, before she and Gyutaro were turned into demons personally by the then Upper Rank Six Doma.

Daki was a tall, curvaceous woman with lime green eyes with a dark orange center, long eyelashes, and very pale skin, complemented by neon pink lips. Her initially black hair was styled in a full, long ponytail with kanzashi hairpins (three on each side on the top, and two on each side on the bottom) holding up the ponytail, along a small, golden comb on the back left side of her hair. The kanji for |Jōgen}} was engraved in Daki's left eye and the daiji for |Roku}} was engraved on the right. Her fingers ended in sharp, dark purple nails. She had a pink obi with black hexagon patterns on all of it, along with light grey blue flower with darker on the center and light orange three length lines on it wrapped around her waist, used as her Blood Demon Art. Her toenails shared the same dark purple color as her fingernails. She sported two pink flower-like demon crests on her face and light purple on the center, one on her cheek and another on her forehead. She also wore a pinkish-red makeup on each sides of the corner of her eyelashes and eyes.

She wore a two-piece version of her kimono consisting of magenta pink panties tied by long, magenta bows on the sides and with two black pieces of cloth with dark magenta flower patterns on the each sides of the cloths that cover her chest with length part than flow reaching her hips. She had black thigh-high stockings with magenta lines on the center of the stocks with the black-flower patterns around them layered with white stockings with one line on each of them and tall, black three-legged sanmaiba, koma-geta or mitsu-ashi shoes. After Daki regains her full power, black cracks appear on various parts of her body and her hair shifts from black to white with lime green tips, matching her original hair color when she was human. When her elder brother Gyutaro awakens, he implants his left eye into Daki's forehead upside-down, creating black ink-like markings (similar to the markings covering Gyutaro's body) around the eye as well.

Under her disguise as an oiran, she appeared to abide to the characteristics of the oiran/tayū, her hair being the typical date-hyōgo style having numerous Ōgi bira kanzashi hairpins both decorating and supporting it as well as wearing traditional makeup. She also hid the flower-like crests on her face. Daki also possessed a multi-colored eye as a further disguise to her demonic nature, with the top half in a terracotta orange color and the bottom half in a lime green color with black thin pupils. She also wore a large white-peach haori with black five-faced pentagonal shaped patterns near the cuffs and hem, with a dark magenta-colored Susohiki/Hikizuri (trailing skirt) kimono and a purple juban under all of it, keeping fragments of her Blood Demon Art as her obi.

entities.name: Doma
entities.description:
Over a century ago, Doma held the position of の|Jōgen no Roku}}, and during that tenure, he turned Gyutaro and Ume into demons and introduced them into the Twelve Kizuki.

He is also the leader of the Eternal Paradise Faith, a cult dedicated to worshipping Doma and a place where he listened to all his followers' troubles and gave them advice. He held this position since he was a human child, and after he became a demon, the cult acted as a place for Doma to gather and kill his victims. This cult also took in Inosuke Hashibira's mother, Kotoha, before Doma killed her after she discovered that he was eating his followers.

Doma is a tall young man of muscular build. He has an extremely pale skin complexion and possessed long, pointed nails that appeared to be stained with a pale purple. He possessed long platinum blond hair that he wore parted to his right; the shorter parts around his face seemed to flare out to either side around his head, curving backwards with one lock slanting down to the right of his face to fall between his eyes, while the longer parts were left to drape centrally down his back in a thinning spiral.

His eyes have been described to be incredibly rare and beautiful, as, in color, they appeared to be made up of an array of rainbow pastel tones, fading into one another as they circle his irises. Along with his platinum blond hair, his unusual appearance even caused people to believe Doma is a blessed being who could communicate with the gods. The kanji for |Jōgen}} is etched across his left eye, and the daiji for |Ni}} or |Roku}} at the time when he first met Gyutaro and Daki on his right, with thick eyelashes and a set of notably thick black eyebrows acting to frame them above.

entities.name: Flute Demon
entities.description:
The |Fue Oni}} was a demon exclusive to the Special One-Shot who desired to join the Twelve Kizuki. He was responsible for the deaths of a small group of Demon Slayers and innocent civilians.

The Flute Demon takes the form of an elderly man with wrinkly skin, and incredibly long black downward-slanted eyebrows. He has long slanted eyes with thin slit pupils and pointed fangs, giving him a rather serpent-like appearance.

His attire consisted of a flower-patterned kataginu-sleeveless robe tied to one side by a white ribbon and long white kimono with a thick black frame at the cuffs. He has long black sashibuki/nu-bakama pants similar in appearance to the Demon Slayer Corps members with geta shoes. As well as this, he wears a black Japanese saggy cap with a tassel at the end.

Like most of his kind, the Flute Demon is murderous and disdainful of humans, happily displaying the corpses of Demon Slayers he had killed and taunting Kyojuro Rengoku by claiming he can join his fallen comrades in the afterlife. He also remarked about his devouring of five children and even joked about one child still alive and cowering before him. He also appears to be very confident in his own abilities and even believed he was destined to join the Twelve Kizuki.

entities.name: Fuku
entities.description:
Fuku is a young girl of a short stature, with long dark brown hair worn in a braid down her back. She has dark purple eyes that fades into a violet color lower down. Her irises are white and vertically rectangular.

Fuku wears a plain red and brown haori over a white-collared shirt, as well as a white kappōgi, which seems to be the uniform of the bento shop she works at. She also wears a tan-colored peaked beret and a pair of large round glasses.

Fuku is a relatively polite girl, albeit one who is often stressed about work and finances. She believes she needs to work hard to support her parents as their business isn't doing very well, something her grandmother tells her is an issue only adults should be worrying about.

Fuki is adamant about her belief that demons don't exist, refusing to turn in for the night just because her grandmother believes they may be vulnerable to demon attacks at night. Once Kyojuro Rengoku slays Slasher before her eyes, however, she rectifies this belief and apologizes to her grandmother for doubting what she'd said.

entities.name: Genya Shinazugawa
entities.description:
Genya is a tall young man with a rough and feral appearance. He is of fair skin tone and muscular build. He has large almond-shaped eyes with dark purple irises, a large, jagged scar that ran over his right cheekbone from his ear to the bridge of his nose, and a furrowed brow, giving him a constant angered expression. He also has numerous scars across his upper body and arms. He has long, black hair in a style of a mohawk with strands framing his neck.

After joining the Demon Slayer Corps, Genya’s outfit consists of a dark olive-green variation of the standard Demon Slayer uniform. This includes a button-up jacket with a stand-up collar and long sleeves, silver buttons, and a shirt pocket on the left breast, with the kanji for |Metsu}} engraved on the back of the uniform. A white long-sleeved collared undershirt is worn beneath the jacket, and the uniform is secured at the waist with a white belt. Over this, Genya wears his signature sleeveless, purple [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yukata yukata], with the lower part of his yukata being a darker color tone. He also wears matching olive-green tattsuke-hakama pants and a pair of white [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jika-tabi jika-tabi] on his feet.

When he made his debut during Final Selection, Genya was shorter, comparable to Tanjiro in stature, and was visibly younger in appearance. His hair was styled into a buzz cut, with only a small clump of messy black hair left to grow on the top of his head as a short mohawk. Genya is seen wearing his purple, sleeveless yukata over a plain black shirt with long sleeves. When they meet again in the Butterfly Mansion, Genya now towers over him while maintaining his outwardly harsh looks and perpetual scowl.

When he meets Tanjiro again in the Swordsmith Village, Genya's physical appearance was less intense and intimidating, with his more youthful features now more prominent. By the time Hashira Training had commenced, his eyes became softer and less wild, and his expression is visible less sullen and harsh, coinciding with his newly gain maturity and sense of camaraderie.

entities.description:
Giichi bears a great resemblance to his ancestor, Giyu. He also has a pale complexion and choppy raven-black, neck-length hair. His haircut is similar to his ancestor's after the battle with Muzan Kibutsuji. His eyes are moderately large, framed by thin eyebrows. The irises a dark blue that fades to a lighter blue with their pupils being bluish-black.

He wears a blue sweater, a pair of black jogging pants with a red stripe on each side, and a black backpack.

Unlike his ancestor Giyu's stoic personality, Giichi seems to be cheerful and happy, especially with his best friends. He also appears to be a generous person, offering his toy charm to his friend when he sees how happy it would make her.

Giichi is with his two best friends from the swimming school walking on the streets, when Sumihiko Kamado runs past them on his way to school.

entities.name: Goto
entities.description:
Goto is a young man of average height, and a rather fit build, as he is able to carry Tanjiro in a fireman hold when ordered to bring him to the Corps Headquarters. Most of his features are blocked by the head covering and the mask all members of the Kakushi adorn, but it is shown he possesses wide, half-moon shaped eyes with brown irises and no pupils. His short hair peeking out from the sides of his head covering are black in color.

Goto's primary personality trait is his sardonic attitude. He has a habit of dryly commenting on the eccentricities of members in the Demon Slayer Corps, whether it be an inward comment in his head, or a blunt and sarcastic statement. Targets of his scorn include the loud, energetic, and aggressive personalties of Zenitsu Agatsuma, Inosuke Hashibira, and Hotaru Haganezuka and superhuman abilties such as Tanjiro and Mitsuri Kanroji's appetite, and the short time in which the former was able to recover from his injuries.

Despite his usually calm personality for his line of work, Goto can have a fiery temper. He angrily yelled at Tanjiro for interrupting the meeting of the Hashira just to get back at one of them, demanding repeatedly for an apology. He also chastised Kanao for not informing anyone that Tanjiro had awakened from his coma, in spite of the respect that he usually has for her.

Goto possesses deep respect for Tanjiro, Inosuke, and Zenitsu because of their capability and bravery. In spite of his sarcasm, he still shows a caring personality for most of his appearances. He is shown to be thoughtful when he delivers castella to Tanjiro after he is comatose from his battle in Yoshiwara, and makes small talk with him after his battle in the Swordsmith Village, even inquiring on the well being of his sister.
