entities.name: Wakuraba
entities.description:
Wakuraba was a man of average stature who had pale and grayish-white skin. He possessed what appeared to be three large cross-shaped scars cut into his cheeks and the center of his forehead, as well as noticeably elf-like, pointed ears. His eyes were wide and sharp with orange irises, with the kanji for |3=Ka}} and the daiji for |San}} etched onto his left eye, signifying his position. He had short black hair and a widow's peak.

Wakuraba wore a dotted, bamboo-colored yukata with a pinstripe pattern, a piece of dark cloth around his waist, and a light cloth around his neck. He also donned two golden hoop earrings on each ear and a pair of wooden sandals with black straps.

Like most of the Lower Ranks, Wakuraba was very loyal to Muzan Kibutsuji. When Muzan brutally executed two of his fellow Lower Ranks, he was in doubt that this would be his end, as he had hoped to become stronger for him. However, Wakuraba appeared to believe in self-preservation above all else and was not just blindly obedient to Muzan. Upon realizing his master had no intentions of sparing a single soul, he resorted to fleeing away from Muzan in an ultimate attempt to survive.

Wakuraba is summoned to the Infinity Castle by Nakime in response to the death of Lower Rank Five, Rui. As the second last to appear, he becomes nervous at the immediate action taken upon him and grows wary of what is to come. Before long, he is transported by Nakime to a platform in front of her, present with him are the rest of the Lower Ranks; Enmu, Rokuro, Mukago, and Kamanue. In front of them stands an unfamiliar looking female demon, causing them to wonder about her identity.

entities.name: Woodland Demon
entities.description:
The |Mori no oni}} was a demon that encountered the young Muichiro and Yuichiro Tokito in their woodland home.

The Woodland Demon was a tall muscular man with pale blue-gray skin and short dark hair. He had two single triangle markings on his shoulders. The ends of his arms were black and had 3 large and sharp fingers on each hand. He wore a brown sleeveless dotted-patterned yukata with dark oval patterns on it, and black hakama pants, held together by a gray sash.

As typical of his kind, the Woodland Demon was cruel, merciless, and unsympathetic to humans, even children, as shown when he gleefully laughed as Yuichiro yelled in pain after having his arm severed off, before angrily telling the Tokito brothers to be quiet when they began to cry in fear, complaining that they were noisy and that no one was going to save them. He also mockingly claims that their lives were meaningless, so it didn't matter whether they existed or not.

On a hot summer night, this demon intruded onto the home of the eleven-year-old Tokito twin brothers, Muichiro and Yuichiro. He at first complained that the only residents were two "brats", but decided to just go for the kill as he approached Muichiro. Yuichiro rushed in to protect his younger brother, but had his left arm severed off as he got caught in the demon's attack. As Yuichiro cried in pain, and Muichiro in fear, the demon began to laugh, but he soon grew irritated at the children's commotion and ordered them to be quiet.

entities.name: Yae
entities.description:
Yae is a young girl of rather short height with dark eyes that tilt slightly inwards, framed by thin eyebrows. She has long, dark hair that reaches down her back, parted to the right with a shoulder-length clump hanging down on either side of her face, which she wears tied back in a low bun.

Yae wears a short, patterned hanten which she fastens with an obiage and buckled belt, and a pale-colored animal skin cloak. She sports a pair of pale nikka zubon pants and shin-high traditional straw fukagutsu boots, and she wears her hunting rifle on a belt around her torso and over her shoulder.

Yae is a stubborn and impatient girl. She demonstrated these traits when the villagers prevented her from seeking revenge on the mountain and when Shinobu informed her about the existence of Demons and Demon Slayers. Nevertheless, disregarding Shinobu's cautionary advice, Yae proceeded to the mountain where she encountered her father, now transformed into a demon. Remarkably, she displayed a sense of responsibility and guilt as she chose to end her own life alongside her father, despite his demonic transformation, as a way of caring for him.

Yae dreamed of becoming a Matagi hunter since childhood, but the people around her had doubts as a female Matagi was unheard of and against their tradition, as it would bring jealousy towards their female goddess Matangi. Her father originally shared these thoughts, however he eventually gave in and decided to train her in the ways of hunting on the condition that she always took it seriously. He taught Yae how to survive on a cold mountain and how to hunt large animals such as bears and deer, and use their carcasses effectively.

entities.name: Yahaba
entities.description:
Yahaba was a young man of average build with pale, gray-tinted skin and very short black hair. He possessed red, cat-like eyes that he normally kept shut. He also had another pair of pale-ringed orange eyes on the palms of his hands, with red upward-pointing arrows on each of the irises and scleras of glowing dark green color.

Yahaba wore a plain olive-green kimono with a brown obi and a dark gray haori, decorated by a strip of green that ran down from his shoulders to his arms and his wrists. He also sported white tabi-socks, a pair of brown zōri with black straps, and an akoya necklace with large blue pearls.

Yahaba was a loyal demon who served only to please his leader, Muzan. Like Susamaru, he wanted Muzan's approval and the chance to become one of the Twelve Kizuki. While he had a sadistic personality, Yahaba preferred to do things in a clean and mature manner; he disliked Susamaru's immature attitude and hated getting himself dirtied.

Even in death, Yahaba regretted being unable to win Muzan's approval and desired only to vindictively slay Tanjiro for rubbing his face in the ground.

entities.name: Yatsu
entities.description:
Yatsu was a short man with an average posture. He had a big forehead and shoulder-length, straight black hair. Ne wore a yellow, vertically-striped haori over a light green kimono and a dark green hakama. Due to his drunkenness, his face was flushed with significant red spots on his forehead and cheeks.

Yatsu was a stubborn, pushy, and aggressive person who displays unruly behavior. Even when he is the one at fault, for instance, when he drunkenly bumps into a stranger, he blames the other individual and isn't satisfied with an apology. He tries to assert dominance over his victim through physical intimidation, by grabbing the victim's shoulders to stop him from leaving the scene, and through verbal intimidation by mocking the victim's clothes and physical appearance.

It doesn't seem like he cares that the victim is physically taller than himself. As his older brother is much taller and bigger than most people, he may be more daring to display his antagonizing behavior since his nearby brother will always be protecting him in case it gets physical. He seems to bear disdain for people from higher classes, as evident by his comments on the quality of Muzan's clothes. He loves drinking, as evidenced by his suggestion for more rounds at bars. Even with a flushed face and poor coordination, he tries to fool himself and his companions into claiming he is not intoxicated.

In Asakusa, Yatsu had been drinking at bars with his older brother and sister-in-law. They are very drunk when they walk through an alleyway. While dancing around, he suggests to his brother to hit up one more bar. When the sister-in-law asks him if he is alright, he says he is fine and not even drunk yet.

entities.name: Yoriichi Tsugikuni
entities.description:
Considered the strongest Demon Slayer to have ever lived, he was the progenitor of Breathing Styles, having created Sun Breathing which would eventually become the Hinokami Kagura used by Tanjiro Kamado and members of the Kamado Family. He was also the first to bear the Demon Slayer Mark, being born with it.

Yoriichi was the younger twin brother of Michikatsu Tsugikuni, who later became a demon and joined the Twelve Kizuki.

Yoriichi was a tall man with a lean, muscular build, fair skin, and maroon eyes. His overall appearance was similar to his twin brother Michikatsu's. Unlike his brother, however, Yoriichi was slightly more slender, had wavier hair, and shorter bangs that framed both sides of his face. His ponytail-tied hair was long, black and red at the tips. Yoriichi was mostly expressionless, though sometimes rather solemn and aloof. As the first person who gained the Demon Slayer Mark, he had blood-red, flame-like patterns on the left of his forehead, which extended down to the side of his temple.

Yoriichi wore a red haori over a pale orange-colored nagagi kimono, a black umanori-styled hakama, and a white uwa-obi. He also wore a pair of zōri with red straps and white tabi socks. Conventional to most Demon Slayers, his Nichirin Sword was carried at the left side of his waist. He sported hanafuda-like earrings created by his mother as charms when he was thought to be deaf; he later gave them to his friend Sumiyoshi Kamado, who then passed the earrings down to his descendants and eventually Tanjiro.

entities.name: Yoshioka
entities.description:
Yoshioka is a male with cropped hair and short bushy eyebrows, similar to Takeuchi. He wears the standard Demon Slayer uniform and has a pale complexion, along with a noticeably round nose.

Not much is known about his personality, but he is impressed by the Hashira's skills.

At a point in his life, Noguchi joined the Demon Slayer Corps.

Yoshioka is first seen undergoing Gyomei Himejima's muscle amplification training while enduring a waterfall with Inosuke Hashibira, Nagakura, and Shimamoto. He is later seen eating and conversing with Murata and Tanjiro while eating fish. He concurs with Murata, Noguchi, Nagakura, and Shimamoto with the sentiment that the reason the current Hashira have no Tsuguko is because they all became frightened by the laborious training. Nevertheless, he enjoys and compliments Tanjiro's cooking, and is even moved to tears by his grilled onigiri.

entities.name: Yoshiteru Agatsuma
entities.description:
Yoshiteru shares a striking resemblance to his great-grandfather Zenitsu Agatsuma, with black pelted hair and arrow shaped eyebrows. He is quite tall in comparison to his friends, as he is seen looming over the other students.

His school uniform consists of a light blue long sleeve shirt, accompanied by a white vest and black tie, as well as black slacks and brown shoes.

Similar to his great-grandfather, Yoshiteru is somewhat exaggerated in regards to his reactions. When he was reading the book which explained the battle against Muzan Kibutsuji, he began crying over his ancestor's determination and willingness to risk their lives.

Yoshiteru has also expressed the flirtatious tendencies of his ancestor as he was seen gawking at female students, as well as being threatened by the reincarnation of Obanai Iguro for staring at his wife's chest, whom was the reincarnation of Mitsuri Kanroji.

entities.name: Yuichiro Tokito
entities.description:
Yuichiro was a short young boy with a fair skin complexion and straight waist-length hair that transitioned from raven-black to turquoise. He wore it loose with two clumps protruding slightly from each side of his head, a set of marginally shorter hair left down to frame his face, and unruly bangs over his forehead. He also possessed large turquoise eyes, a trait, like his hair, that he shared with his twin brother Muichiro.

He wore a sleeveless yukata that was black with a light blue mist design, similar to the one his brother wore when they were both ten, albeit Muichiro's was lighter in color.

Yuichiro was a cold and skeptical individual who didn't believe in compassion or caring for others. He believed that doing good deeds wouldn't do a person a shred of good, which is seen when he claimed his father was a fool for dying while trying to gather herbs to help cure his mother's fatal illness, and shot down Muichiro's suggestion that they become Demon Slayers in order to save people's lives. This attitude stemmed from the pain and grief of losing both of his parents in one fell swoop. However, just before he succumbed from his wounds in a demon's attack, Yuichiro was seen praying that his brother be saved and apologizing for getting in his way when he wanted to be useful, showing that deep down he truly did try to see the worth of good done by people.

Yuichiro's critical attitude to the altruism his parents' selflessness and their good intentions to help others while neglecting their own limitations was not entirely true. It was something that Yuichiro likely spoke to his brother out of fear that the same fate would befall him. However, when Yuichiro jumped in front of his brother to protect him, it became clear that he is more similar to his family than he imagined.

entities.name: Yushiro
entities.description:
During the final confrontation with Muzan Kibutsuji, Yushiro, along with Tamayo, joins forces with the Demon Slayer Corps to aid the Demon Slayers.

Yushiro has the appearance of a young man of short stature and average build with pale skin and sharp, lavender eyes with black slit pupils. He has short hair that is neatly styled and vertically shaded from a mint green to black.

Yushiro wears a light blue-grey button-up collared shirt under an all-white iromuji-haori and dark blue Seigo-Sendeihira styled hakama pants. He wears pair of [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z%C5%8Dri zōri] with dark blue straps and white [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabi tabi socks].

When disguising himself as a Demon Slayer, he dons their standard black uniform, tinted green in the anime. The uniform consisted of a button-up jacket with a stand-up collar and long sleeves, featuring silver buttons, a shirt pocket on the left breast, and the kanji for |Metsu}} engraved on the back of the uniform. Beneath the jacket, he wears a white long-sleeved collared undershirt. He wears a matching tattsuke-hakama pants, and secured with a white belt. He wears green tabi socks and pair of zōri sandals with white straps. He also conceals his slit pupils similar to Tamayo. On his back, he carries a white backpack with medical supplies inside.

entities.name: Asakusa
entities.description:
It is a large, heavily populated urban center with tall buildings and bright lights that illuminate the city during the night. Many people walk through crowded marketplaces with dozens of business signs. Unlike Tanjiro Kamado's small town, there are cars of carriages guiding citizens through the roads. There is also a trolley system that runs throughout the city. The city sits on a bay decorated with a large fountain tower next to a large body of water.

Muzan Kibutsuji lived here under the guise of a human along with his wife and daughter and it is the base of operations for him. Lady Tamayo and Yushiro lived in a cloaked house in the city until they were discovered by Muzan's servants, Susamaru and Yahaba.

entities.name: Butterfly Mansion
entities.description:
The |Chō Yashiki}} is the manor that the late Flower Hashira Kanae Kocho, Insect Hashira Shinobu Kocho, Tsuguko Kanao Tsuyuri, and assistants Aoi Kanzaki, Sumi Nakahara, Kiyo Terauchi, and Naho Takada live in. The manor is often used as a recovery base for injured Demon Slayers.

The majority of healing at the mansion is done by Shinobu Kocho, though there are also attendants known as Kakushi who run errands and assist in watching over the injured. On top of this, there are others who live in the mansion that are not Demon Slayers, but offer training regiments to facilitate the recovery process and help the injured Demon Slayers reach top condition again. For example, Aoi Kanzaki creates a training regiment meant to help Tanjiro Kamado, Inosuke Hashibira, and Zenitsu Agatsuma recover after their battles on Mount Natagumo.

After Nezuko Kamado became the first demon to conquer the sun, she was relocated to the Butterfly Mansion for her protection with Sakonji Urokodaki as her caretaker. In addition Kiriya, Kuina, and Kanata Ubuyashiki were stationed at the mansion to prepare and aid for the eventual battle against Muzan Kibutsuji, and to keep tabs on the corps when they were forced inside the Infinity Castle using Kasugai Crows and Yushiro's Blood Demon Art. Former-Hashira Tengen Uzui and Shinjuro Rengoku acted as bodyguards and Suma was also present at the mansion but her role is unknown.

The first Flower Breathing user planted the cherry blossom tree in the garden of the Butterfly Mansion, and gave it the name "Victory Tree". After the final battle against Muzan Kibutsuji, Kanao Tsuyuri visited the tree to tell it that they are victorious.

entities.name: Eternal Paradise Faith
entities.description:
The |Bansei Gokuraku Kyō}} was a centuries-old cult dedicated to worshipping Upper Rank Two Doma.

The Eternal Paradise Faith was formed by Doma's parents as a way for their child to give guidance to its followers from "supposedly" hearing the voices of gods. Later on, after becoming a demon, it became a way for Doma to amass followers in order to kill and eat them. He did this not only to satiate his own demon biology, but also because as an atheist who believed the gods and the afterlife to be a foolish fantasies, Doma believed that consuming his followers allowed them to be "saved" and live on with him forever.

The cult was located in a shrine with several lotus iconography, with Doma being surrounded by a bed of lotuses. However, Doma was also shown to have his own palace surrounded by a large water garden with endless pathways inside the Infinity Castle. Given that Doma was shown dining on several female disciples on the pathways, it is possible that the location inside the secret demon fortress was where Doma's followers met their demise. In addition, Doma was known to collect the decomposed heads of his victims, using a pot gifted to him by Upper Rank Five Gyokko to display one.

Since Doma was the self-proclaimed founder and the cult was started around him in the first place, Doma was the main figure of worship. After his transformation however, as a show of loyalty to the Demon King, Muzan Kibutsuji was made another figure of worship, this time as a deity to be revered. Moreover, the cult's membership was limited to a total of 250 members, as Doma would get scolded for standing out too much.

entities.name: Kirimise
entities.description:
Attempting to inform her husband, Hinatsuru poisoned herself in order to escape Daki's surveillance and is sent to one of the Kirimise Houses as an attempt to escape. However, Daki's obi held Hinatsuru hostage and she is left unable to escape.

After interrogating the master of the Kyogoku House for her whereabouts, Tengen Uzui enters the Kirimise and is able to locate Hinatsuru, ill and still bound in the obi. He cuts her free and gives her an antidote, whilst she explains why she was unable to contact him. Telling him to leave her and fight the demon, Hinatsuru is hugged by Tengen before he leaves for battle, leaving her to heal.

Eventually, Hinatsuru gains enough strength to leave the Kirimise to join the battle. It is unknown whether the area was destroyed at the end of the battle, though it is very likely it was, given the immense range and power of Gyutaro's final attack.

entities.name: Kyogoku House
entities.description:
The |Kyōgoku ya}} is a traditional Japanese brothel located in the Entertainment District of Tokyo, Japan.

It is not known when the Kyogoku House was established in Entertainment District. However, when Tengen Uzui was investigating the report of a demon within the district, he sends his wife, Hinatsuru, to infiltrate the Kyogoku House to try and gather information.

After he loses contact with his wife, Tengen travels to the Entertainment District with the Demon Slayers to try to infiltrate a second time. After Tanjiro and Inosuke are dropped off at their corresponding houses, Zenitsu is abandoned at the Kyogoku house by Tengen (disguised as Zenko).

It is revealed that two days before the Demon Slayer's arrived at the district, the demon, Daki, had been discovered living within the house by Omitsu, the headmistress, and seemingly murdered her.

entities.name: Mount Fujikasane
entities.description:
The mountain is used by the Demon Slayer Corps for the Final Selection, where individuals seeking to become an official Demon Slayer can prove themselves. The examinees that pass shall be recognized and receive their own Demon Slayer Uniform, Nichirin Sword and Kasugai Crows.

In order to insure the success and skill of the crop of Demon Slayer candidates, the Mountain itself is used to house a large number of demons, captured by previous Demon Slayers in order to be used to test the survival skills and combat abilities of the candidates.

Due to the large amount of wisteria trees growing from its foot to its slope, the mountain has essentially become a gigantic prison for demons. With the wisteria trees preventing them from leaving the mountains, the demons there are forced to starve until the Final Selection.

During his time as a active Demon Slayer, former Water Hashira, Sakonji Urokodaki, captured an initially weak demon and imprisoned it in the mountain to use him in the Final Selection. However, unknown to him, this demon would thrive and gain power and strength in the mountain by feasting on the Demon Slayer candidates for 47 years. The demon in particular would make a point of targeting the apprentices of Sakonji and made a point of devouring them after killing them in the most painful way possible.

entities.name: Mount Kumotori
entities.description:
After his mother died from illness when he was ten years old, Yoriichi Tsugikuni fled from his home. He ran straight for one day and one night without any sign of exhaustion. Eventually, he arrived at a place full of compact fields and paddies on Mount Kumotori. There, he met Uta, a girl of similar age who had tragically lost her entire family to a a widespread illness. Yoriichi made the decision to reside with Uta in her humble mountain hut, and over the course of ten years, their bond deepened, culminating in their marriage. During Uta's final month of pregnancy, Yoriichi left their home in order to summon a midwife to ensure a safe delivery for the child, hopeful to return before the sun set. On his way, Yoriichi encountered a feeble old man struggling to traverse the mountain. The man's son had been gravely wounded in battle, and Yoriichi chose to accompany the man so that he could see his son's final moments. He decided to fetch the midwife the next day. By then the sun had already set and when he finally arrived home as fast as he could, he found that Uta and the unborn child were killed by a demon. The tragedy shocked Yoriichi so much that he absentmindedly embraced her corpse for ten days straight and only buried them after a pursuing Demon Slayer, a Rengoku ancestor, encouraged him to do so. Yoriichi's dream for a peaceful life with his wife and child were tragically shattered by the existence of demons in the world. Driven by sorrow and a resolute purpose, Yoriichi decided to embark on a new path as a Demon Slayer, leaving behind his home in Mount Kumotori.

Years later, newlyweds Sumiyoshi Kamado and Suyako Kamado stumble upon an abandoned hut on Mount Kumotori. Unbeknownst to them, this humble abode was once inhabited by Yoriichi and Uta. After Yoriichi's fateful encounter with Muzan Kibutsuji and subsequent exile from the Demon Slayer Corps, he returned to the house he once shared with his late wife. There, he ran into Sumiyoshi and Suyako, who was on the last month of her pregnancy, as they were being attacked by a demon. Without hesitation, Yoriichi rescued them from the demon. Afterwards, Suyako started going into labor and Yoriichi left to summon a midwife with unprecedented speed. The next day, Suyako successfully gave birth to a baby girl named Sumire Kamado. In the act of aiding this young couple, Yoriichi found a semblance of redemption, a bittersweet solace for his own unfulfilled longing for a family with his late wife.

The Spider Family attempts to live in peace on the mountain and whenever anyone approaches them, the family attacks the intruders and kills them. The mountain is ruled by Rui, Lower Rank Five of the Twelve Kizuki, and also the head of the Spider Family. Rui makes sure that all of his family members are doing their tasks to keep the family safe.

entities.name: Ogimoto House
entities.description:
The |Ogimoto ya}} is a traditional Japanese brothel located in the Entertainment District of Tokyo, Japan.

It is not known when the Ogimoto House was established in Entertainment District. However, when Tengen Uzui was investigating the report of a demon within the district, he sends his wife, Makio, to infiltrate the Ogimoto House to try and gather information.

After he loses contact with his wife, Tengen travels to the Entertainment District with the Demon Slayer's to try to infiltrate a second time. When they are walking on the street, the madam of the Ogimoto household coincidentally bumps into Inosuke Hashibira (disguised as Inoko), and offers to take her in as a courtesan.

After settling into the house, Inosuke begins to investigate the whereabouts of Makio, and overhears a rumor that she has been sick and stuck in her room. Unbeknownst to him, Makio was being held captive by Daki's sentient Obi sash which was spying on her and holding her captive.

entities.name: Soryu Dojo
entities.description:
The |Soryū Dōjō}} was a martial arts center owned solely by Keizo. His only known student and later heir was a young orphan named Hakuji.

The dojo and its surrounding land originally belonged to an old man. After he was saved from bandits by Keizo, who used a bare-fist martial arts fighting style, he decided to give Keizo ownership out of gratitude and awe at his abilities, and also because he didn't have an heir. Keizo moved in with his sickly daughter Koyuki, and possibly his wife, who drowned herself out of despair from nursing her, as she didn't believe she would recover.

Keizo was frequently harassed by a neighboring dojo that wanted the land for themselves, and because of this Keizo had trouble finding students, instead making a living through odd jobs. After hearing that a child was going to be killed after going on a bloody rampage, Keizo personally subdued him and took him in as a student, while also commanding him to be Koyuki's caretaker. The boy, Hakuji, reluctantly agreed and would frequently spend his time either nursing Koyuki or training with Keizo.

There was an incident with the rivaling dojo; the young heir who had a crush on Koyuki pressured her to go outside despite her illness, causing her to violently cough. The panicked and fled, and Koyuki was saved by Hakuji, who was infuriated. The result was a feud between the two dojos; Keizo was on standby while Hakuji defeated nine students, forbidding further interaction between Koyuki and the dojo. After Hakuji defeated the heir who attempted to attack with a real sword, the owner of the rival dojo accepted defeat and stopped bothering the Soryu dojo.

entities.name: Swordsmith Village
entities.description:
The の|Katanakaji no Sato}} is the titular location of the Swordsmith Village Arc. It is a secretive settlement nestled within a dense forest. The hidden village serves as a hub for the creation and forging of weapons exclusively for Demon Slayers.

The village is home to the swordsmiths who forge weapons, notably the Nichirin Swords, for members of the Demon Slayer Corps.

To safeguard the village from Demon attacks, strict measures are taken to keep the place concealed and its exact location is kept confidential. Demon Slayers who wish to visit the village must travel blindfolded, with their ears and noses plugged, while piggybacking a Kakushi, to prevent information from being leaked to the demons. After some time, the travelers are passed from one Kakushi to another. Furthermore, the routes and Kakushi themselves are frequently changed. Even the Kakushi who transport the travelers remain unaware of the village's precise location. Guided by Kasugai Crows, each Kakushi is directed to the next in line, although even these crows are switched constantly.

All inhabitants of the village are commonly seen wearing variations of hyottoko masks in order to keep their identity concealed, a tactic used to protect them from being tracked.

entities.name: Tokito House
entities.description:
The |Tokito ya}} is a traditional Japanese brothel located in the Entertainment District of Tokyo, Japan.

It is not known when the Tokito House was established in the Entertainment District. However, when Tengen Uzui was investigating the report of a demon within the district, he sends his wife, Suma, to infiltrate the Tokito House to try and gather information.

After he loses contact with his wife, Tengen travels to the Entertainment District with the Demon Slayers to try to infiltrate a second time. Tengen presents the Demon Slayers, crudely dressed in makeup, to the Tokito house, hoping one of them will be taken in and begin the mission. Though the owners are shocked at their appearance, the house's madam happily agrees to take one in, taken aback by Tengen's handsomeness. Tanjiro (disguised as Sumiko) is taken. At first, the madam is furious that Tengen tricked him after finding out Tanjiro has a scar on his head and yells how she's going to get customers with him. But she gets her heart won over because Tanjiro is good at doing various chores.

As Tanjiro lifts a set of gifts to Koinatsu, he overhears some girls talking about Suma doing 'Ashinuke': the act of a prostitute leaving her home without paying her debts over love. Koinatsu interrupts their chat, telling them to stop spreading rumors. Tanjiro asks about Suma's whereabouts to Koinatsu. Koinatsu is suspicious of Tanjiro's intention and asks him whats his connection with Suma is. Realizing this, Tanjiro attempts to lie and claim that Suma is his older sister and enters the district looking for her. Tanjiro assures them that Suma wouldn't have left suddenly. Koinatsu confirms it and comments that Suma was seemingly a grounded girl without any hint of being in love with a man.

entities.description:
The の|Tsuzumi no Yashiki}} is a large house controlled by Kyogai located in the south-southeast. It is the titular setting of the Tsuzumi Mansion Arc.

The Tsuzumi Mansion was originally Kyogai's home while he was a human and has been his base of operations since transforming into a demon. Each room is controlled by Kyogai's Blood Demon Art in different ways. They can be flipped different directions or anyone inhabiting them can be transferred between rooms. While Kyogai's Blood Demon Art is active, running around the hallways of the mansion will only lead someone in circles.

Tanjiro Kamado and Zenitsu Agatsuma arrive at the mansion after being given orders to defeat the demon who lives there. They bump into a pair of siblings who ask them to help find their brother, as well as Inosuke Hashibira.

entities.name: Ubuyashiki Mansion
entities.description:
The grand mansion served as the residence of the Taisho era's Oyakata, Kagaya Ubuyashiki, his wife Amane, and children, and it had been in the possession of the Ubuyashiki Family for generations.

It was located on the top of a mountain in a secluded and well-protected area to ensure the safety of its residents and visitors. Its precise location was kept secret to protect against demon attacks. Compared to the already obscure and hidden Swordsmith Village, even more complicated methods were used to hide the estate.

The mansion was traditional in design, featuring elegant wooden architecture. A wooden veranda ran along the perimeter of the house, slightly elevated from the ground and served as a transitional space between the indoors and the garden. The mansion's surroundings were serene and peaceful. It had a beautifully well-maintained Zen garden, and the ground of this garden was primarily covered by white gravel. The garden featured wisteria trees, bonsai trees, stone lanterns and a pond with large Ishi stones around it. The entire plot of land was surrounded by an engawa.

The head of the Ubuyashiki family lead the Demon Slayer Corps from this estate. The mansion served as the hub for strategic planning where key decisions were made and where the efforts against demons were coordinated. Important meetings and strategy sessions were held at the estate, particularly in the presence of the Hashira, the Corps' most powerful swordsmen. These gatherings were crucial for planning missions and discussing tactics for their next moves in combating the demon threat.

entities.name: Yoshiwara
entities.description:
Yoshiwara was founded in the Edo period of Japan, where it quickly became a prominent district for prostitution and other sex work. The highest ranking courtesans were known as Oirans. Three of the most famous and prominent pleasure houses in the district during the Taisho period were the Tokito House, Kyogoku House, and Ogimoto House.

For about a century, before the latest intervention of the Demon Slayer Corps, Yoshiwara became the home and the lair of two extremely powerful demons: the siblings Daki and Gyutaro, the dual holders of the position of Upper Rank Six of the Twelve Kizuki. Owing to Daki's great beauty, experience in sex work, and her unique Blood Demon Art, they made Yoshiwara a successful hunting ground, where they captured and devoured numerous victims over the years. Daki's nigh-immortality and subsequent attempts to hide her true nature started the urban legend of a incredibly beautiful but also incredibly cruel Oiran, the stories passing down generations. Most attempts to stop them by the Demon Slayer Corps were unsuccessful, with Gyutaro having killed 15 Hashira and Daki having killed 7.

During the Taisho Period, Sound Hashira Tengen Uzui was given the mission of hunting down the demonic presence in Yoshiwara and sent in his three wives, Hinatsuru, Makio, and Suma, to infiltrate the three most prominent pleasure houses in the Entertainment District and search for clues on his behalf. When all three suddenly stopped providing him with information, Tengen began his own investigation to save them and find the demon himself.

Tengen attempted to take Aoi Kanzaki and Naho Takada as he needed female Demon Slayers to accompany him. His forcible abduction of the two was stopped by Kanao Tsuyuri, Sumi Nakahara, Kiyo Terauchi, and Tanjiro Kamado, who then proposed to accompany him on his mission instead, alongside his partners Zenitsu Agatsuma and Inosuke Hashibira. Satisfied with three willing Demon Slayers, Tengen began the mission to save his wives and the people of Yoshiwara.
